newsitem.title: USA: EPA approves long-term plan for Louisiana estuary.
newsitem.headline: EPA approves long-term plan for Louisiana estuary.

text.p: The Environmental Protection Agency Friday approved a long-term plan to clean up Louisiana's 4 million-acre Barataria-Terrebonne Estuary.

The estuary, between the Mississippi and Atchafalay rivers, contains more coastal wetlands than any other U.S. estuary, but it is disappearing quickly from the effects of development and attempts to change natural water flows.
About half an acre of coastal land turns to open water every 15 minutes, the EPA said. Since 1932 the area has lost more than 656 square miles of productive wetlands and barrier islands, it said.
"Today's plan will provide vital protection for this coastal area in ways that make economic and environmental sense for the people of Louisiana," EPA Administrator Carol Browner said in a statement.
The plan deals with changes in water flows, reduced sediment flows, loss of wildlife habitat and pollution, the EPA said.
